title: The wire: machines types
description: Part of the source of every type on the wire (#1135, #5380): one file per domain in Packages/Wire/schema. A $ref to another file names it (core.schema.json#/definitions/JSONValue); scripts/wire.sh gen reads them all.

AgentMachines.description: machines/forAgent: what list_machines shows an agent.

hosts.description: Every machine of the person's, by name, where start_session can start a session (#2887). Absent from an older control plane.

capacity.description: The machine's capacity level as it last pushed it (#5875), so an agent does not start heavy work on a full machine. Absent before its first push.

loadPerCore5.description: Its 5-minute load per core when it last pushed.

capacityAt.description: When the control plane last heard its capacity. A figure older than 2 minutes is no figure (Auto's rule).

platform.description: The machine's platform as it announced it (macOS 15, Linux), so Autopilot (#5900) sends a linux-ok issue to a Linux machine. Absent when it did not say.

reason.description: Why it failed, on a make that failed (#4706).

addresses.description: Its public addresses, IPv4 then IPv6, from the provider's own record (#7466).

AgentsChange.description: One change in Agents between two versions (#5273): a commit of agentloops-dev/agent-loops, its PR's number when its squash title says one, its title (the first line of its message) and when it was made.

AgentsChanges.description: The changes in Agents from version base to version head (#5273), from GitHub's compare of their commits: ahead is how many commits head has that base has not, behind how many base has that head has not (a machine behind another). changes are head's new commits, newest first, at most the request's limit (all, up to 1,000, with none); complete is false when there were more.

AgentsChangesRequest.description: machines/agentsChanges (#5273): the changes from one Agents version to another, as a machine says them (0.18.0, 0.18.1-dev.544+g8162a5a06). limit bounds the changes; with none, all, up to 1,000.

AnnounceReply.description: What devices/announce answers: the device's record.

AutoMachineNone.description: Why no machine fits: none has the project, none has the runtime installed and signed in, or every machine with the project is offline.

AutoMachinePick.description: The answer of sessions/previewStart (#5374): the pick, or why none fits. The control plane makes the reason line; a client draws what it is given. The pick at start may differ if the state moved.

machine.description: The machine chosen; absent when none fits.

tier.description: The tier the pick came from.

loadPerCore.description: Its 5-minute load per core, when known.

commit.description: The commit the session's fresh worktree starts from. Set by the host at start; absent in a preview.

text.description: The one-line reason, "Auto chose Mac mini: you last started here.", or the none-fits sentence.

offline.description: With none offline: the names of the offline machines that have the project.

single.description: True when the project has one machine only: no Auto row and no line, the machine is just shown.

AutoMachineReason.description: Why Auto chose: the person last started this project there, or it was the least loaded by 5-minute load per core.

AutoMachineRequest.description: sessions/previewStart and a start with machine auto (#5374, specs/5373-auto-machine): which machine Auto would pick for a project and a runtime.

wait.description: Answer once the backup is made, not at once: a provider's delete waits for it (#1815).

target.description: Where backups go (#1815): this machine's folder, or the control plane's store. Left out is the machine's default: the store for a server linked to a control plane, else the folder.

canUseControl.description: The machine is linked to a control plane, so it can back up to the control plane's store (#1815).

sameDisk.description: The backup folder is on the disk of what it backs up, and not a synced folder (#2139): a backup there undoes a mistake, but is lost with the disk.

BackupStoreCommit.description: A host's backup whose parts are all uploaded: the control plane writes its .json last, then keeps the newest keep of this host's (#1815).

BackupStorePart.description: One part of a backup, at most 8 MiB (#1815): a host's upload, or the control plane's answer to a download.

name.description: On an upload, the backup's name; this host's own folder is the control plane's to say.

BranchFromRequest.description: agents/branchFrom (#1658): a new session that goes on from just before the person's prompt `entryID` in `agentID`.

BringBack.description: What folders/bringBack did (#1473): the branches that moved forward or were made, and whether the uncommitted changes were applied.

BringBackFromRequest.description: folders/bringBackFrom (#4640): Bring Back from ‹machine›… from a client. This host brings `branches` of the repository at `source` on `machine` (the control plane's id or name for it; `machineName` is the name the person knows it by, for the words), less the commits it has, and with `includeChanges` the uncommitted changes there, into the repository at `folder` here, through the control plane, as bring_back does (#2947). Branches move forward only.

BringBackNotification.description: bringBack/changed (#4640): how a bring-back that folders/bringBackFrom started goes. `read` of `total` bytes are here (0 of 0 while the bundle is made there); `finished` once it ended, whichever way: `result` is what it did, or `problem` says why it stopped, in the person's words.

BringBackRequest.description: Brings a host's branches back into this Mac's repository at `folder` (Bring back from ‹host›…, #1473): fetches the `bundle` upload, moves `branches` forward only, also where a worktree has one checked out, and applies the `patch` upload (the host's uncommitted changes) in `folder`, whose checked-out branch must be `patchOn`. It stops, and changes nothing, when a branch here has commits of its own or a worktree with a branch that moves has uncommitted changes.

BringBackSummary.description: One bring-back folders/bringBackFrom started (#4640): the folder here, and the folder on the machine it comes from.

CapacityLevel.description: A machine's capacity (#4578): ok; near (load per core above 1.5, or memory pressure warn); or full (load per core above 2.5, memory pressure critical, or swap more than half used). It rises at once, and falls only after two looks under its line.

CapacityReason.description: What put a machine near or at capacity (#6596): cpu (its load per core), memory (critical memory pressure) or disk (disk pressure, #7300). It stays while the level waits to fall. Absent at ok.

CapacityReport.description: machine/capacity (#5374): a host tells the control plane its capacity level and 5-minute load per core, on connect and when either moves enough to matter.

CapacityState.description: capacity/state and capacity/changed (#4748): the machine's level, pushed when it moves, so a machine's row says it with no page open.

words.description: The level as a sentence's subject and verb: "this Mac is near capacity" or "this Mac is at capacity". Absent at ok.

CatchUpPart.description: A part this host does not know is left out of CatchUpRequest.parts.

ClientKind.description: ClientRecord.Kind: a kind a later build added reads as `unknown`.

ClientPairingRequest.description: clients/startPairing: `browser` for the web remote's code (071); a grant an older window sends is not read.

ClientRecord.description: A paired screen, as clients/list says it (ClientRecord).

ConnectionsListAll.description: connections/listAll (#5592): each machine's connections/list. unreached is the machines that have the method but did not answer (offline, too slow or an error); notAsked counts the machines past the most one call asks (50), as in DocsListAll.

ControlCapacityCopy.description: One live control plane copy's most recent capacity look (#6590).

machine.description: The id of the machine record that runs this copy (#6609, #6591): the row in Machines it is the level of. Absent from an older copy, and from a hosted copy, which has no machine record.

ControlEligible.description: control/eligible's answer (#6611): ok when there are no reasons.

address.description: Where the control plane reached the machine's control role, as a person reads it (#7313): its domain, or its public address, with the port when it is not 443. Absent when it did not reach it there, or reached it by its tunnel.

memoryBytes.description: The machine's memory, as it said it (#7313). Absent when it did not say.

diskFreeBytes.description: The free space on its fullest disk, as it said it (#7313). Absent when it did not say.

frozenSeconds.description: About how long a move to the machine keeps the control plane frozen, in seconds, from the store's size and the copy's batches (#7395). Changes are refused while it is frozen. Absent from a control plane before #7395.

ControlEligibleReason.description: One reason a machine cannot take the control role (#6611), with its words for the person.

ControlEligibleRequest.description: control/eligible (#6611): which machine, and what the person has said yes to.

allowSleep.description: The person says yes to a control plane on a Mac, which can sleep. It counts only in the single-user shape.

ControlIneligibility.description: Why a machine cannot take the control role (#6611): notReachable, the control plane cannot reach it at a public address or its tunnel; macSleeps, a Mac that sleeps (refused unless the shape is single-user and the person says yes); stopsWhenIdle, its provider stops it when it is idle; belowFloor, its memory or disk is below the floor, or it is near or at capacity; bothRoles, it runs agents and the shape is not single-user; olderVersion, it runs an older version than the control plane.

ControlMove.description: One move of the control plane to another machine (#6612, epic #6608), as v1/moves/<id>.json keeps it: at most 20, for 90 days. At most one runs at a time.

from.description: The copy that moves: its id.

toName.description: The machine's name when the move started.

failedPhase.description: With failed: the step that failed.

address.description: Where the new copy answers, once it said so.

copied.description: With copying: the records copied so far (#7395). control/moveChanged says it every few seconds during the copy.

total.description: With copying: the records the copy takes (#7395).

forwardingUntil.description: With forwarding: until when the old copy sends members to the new one (30 days at most).

error.description: With failed: what went wrong, in words. The old copy serves again.

ControlMovePhase.description: Where a move stands (#6612), in this order: checking, control/eligible's checks; receiving, the new machine is given the control key, sealed to its own key, and starts a copy that is empty; frozen, the old copy changes no record; copying, the store goes to the new copy; forwarding, the new copy took over and the old one sends members to it (30 days at most); done, the new copy took over at the old address. failed: a step failed, and the old copy serves again.

ControlMoveRequest.description: control/move (#6612): the machine to move the control plane to.

ControlMoveResult.description: control/move's answer: the move, started. control/moveChanged says each step after.

ControlMoves.description: control/moves/list (#6612): the newest moves first, at most 20.

ControlReceive.description: control/receive's answer: where the machine's copy answers now, empty and receiving, and its certificate's pin when it has its own.

ControlReceiveRequest.description: control/receive (#6612): the control plane asks a machine with the control role to start its copy empty, to receive a move. The control key is sealed to the machine's own key, with the move, the machine and the control key's public half as its associated data.

url.description: The address that clients reach the machine at, as control/eligible found it.

DetectedServer.description: One host in the ssh config, and what machines/detect did with it (#429).

DocsListAll.description: docs/listAll (#5571): a page of docs from the caller's machines, the last updated first, each with its machine. unreached is the machines that have docs but did not answer (offline or too slow); their docs are not in docs. sources are those of the machines that answered this page: the first page has every machine's. notAsked counts the machines past the most one call asks (50). cursor is the next page, absent at the end.

DocsListAllRequest.description: docs/listAll (#5571): the docs of the caller's machines in one call. limit is 1 to 500, 200 when not said; it bounds the page, not each machine, and a cursor goes with the same limit. source narrows to one DocsSource id.

cursor.description: Opaque: the last page's cursor, as the answer gave it. Absent for the first page.

EventsListAll.description: events/listAll (#5592): each machine's newest EventsPage. unreached is the machines that have the method but did not answer (offline, too slow or an error); notAsked counts the machines past the most one call asks (50), as in DocsListAll.

EventsListAllRequest.description: events/listAll (#5592): the newest page of each of the caller's machines' events/list in one call. limit is each machine's, as in EventsListRequest, 50 when not said, at most 100. An older page is one machine's, by events/list.

FeatureUsageAll.description: reports/featuresAll (#5592): each machine's reports/features. unreached is the machines that have the method but did not answer (offline, too slow or an error); notAsked counts the machines past the most one call asks (50), as in DocsListAll.

FirstBuildStartRequest.description: firstBuild/start (#5056, spec 5048 section 7): the newcomer's idea, as typed, the starter the plan page shows, and the runtime its first task set up. The host makes the folder ~/.agents/first-build when it is not there, writes the first prompt itself, so every client sends the same, and labels the session first-build. It answers with the session's id. While a first-build session that is not archived is there, it refuses with firstBuildRunning, with that session's id as the data, unless another is true (New App…, #5132).

idea.description: The person's words, as typed. Not empty.

runtimeID.description: The runtime that the plan page's first task set up, as agents/start takes it.

another.description: New App… (#5132): start one more first build, also while a first-build session is there. Absent or false keeps the newcomer's rule: refuse with firstBuildRunning.

FirstBuildStarter.description: The starter that a first build begins from (#5048): iphone-app is agentloops-dev/iphone-app-starter, web-service is agentloops-dev/web-service-starter, as make_app_repository names them.

FleetBoard.description: console/fleet's answer (#1804): every machine on the control plane, for an admin.

FleetMachine.description: One machine on Console ▸ Machines (#1804): its machines/list row, whose it is, and how many of its agents were running when it last listed them. Numbers only, never what the agents said.

ownerName.description: Its person's or bot's name; empty when nobody owns it.

bot.description: Whether its owner is a bot (#1761).

running.description: Its agents running when it last listed them; absent when it never has.

heardAt.description: When it last listed its agents.

ForgeBoardsAll.description: forge/boardsAll (#5592): each machine's forge/boards. unreached is the machines that have the method but did not answer (offline, too slow or an error); notAsked counts the machines past the most one call asks (50), as in DocsListAll.

ForgeListAll.description: forge/listAll (#5592): each machine's ForgeList, as it answered, in the order of the caller's machines. The machines list the same repos, so a client merges the items by ref. unreached is the machines that have the method but did not answer (offline, too slow or an error); notAsked counts the machines past the most one call asks (50), as in DocsListAll.

ForgeListAllRequest.description: forge/listAll (#5592): forge/issues (kind issues) or forge/pulls (kind pulls) of the caller's machines in one call. state, board, label, assignee (a login), sort and limit are as in ForgeListRequest, for each machine (label and assignee: #6383; sort: #6538). pages, for a next page, names the machines to ask and each one's cursor, as its last list gave it; without pages every machine is asked for its first page.

sort.description: The order, as in ForgeListRequest (#6538): priority, else the last updated first; each machine sorts its own list.

fresh.description: As in ForgeListRequest (#6642): each machine reads its forges, not its kept answer. A Refresh.

LineageForecastAll.description: lineage/forecastAll (#5592): each machine's lineage/forecast for the same request. unreached is the machines that have the method but did not answer (offline, too slow or an error); notAsked counts the machines past the most one call asks (50), as in DocsListAll.

MacPathRequest.description: mac/reveal, mac/open: a path on the host; app names the app to open it with.

MacTerminalRequest.description: mac/terminal: Terminal, in path if given.

MachineAgents.description: machines/agents (#5273, spec 5239 board 6): a machine page's Agents section. version is what the machine runs, since the first machine/hello at it; previous is the version before. changes are the changes since previous, the newest few (machines/agentsChanges gives all); absent when there is no previous or GitHub could not say, and changesError says why in the second case. history is the versions it ran, newest first, at most 20. others are the person's other machines, each with its version.

MachineAgentsOther.description: Another of the person's machines on a machine's page (#5273): its version, since when, and how many changes it is ahead of and behind the page's machine. ahead and behind are absent when GitHub could not say (a version with no commit, GitHub not answering).

MachineAgentsVersion.description: One version a machine ran (#5273) and when it came: the first machine/hello at it.

roles.description: What the machine does (#6609, #7314): agents, control or both, from its install. Absent means agents. A machine with control alone runs no agents: it keeps a link for the store copy and the handover, and the control plane opens no client's channel to it.

MachineClient.description: A paired window a host may let in on its local socket (#1118), with the key it proves itself with.

person.description: The person the window belongs to (#994). The host lets it in only when it is the host's own user (FR-020).

MachineClients.description: machine/clients: every window paired with the control plane, which a host checks its local socket against (#1118).

user.description: The user the host belongs to (#994). With it, the host lets in only a window whose person is that user (FR-020); without it (an older control plane), every window listed.

MachineControlAddress.description: Where a machine's control role serves (#7313): the domain its certificate is for, when it has one, and the port. With no domain, the control plane dials the public address that the machine's uplink comes from.

port.description: From 1 to 65535; a hello with another is taken as none.

MachineConversation.description: A conversation of messages/conversationsAll (#5571) with the machine whose connector has it.

MachineCursor.description: A machine and the cursor of its next page (#5592).

MachineDoc.description: A doc of docs/listAll (#5571) with the machine that has it.

MachineDocsSource.description: A source of docs/listAll (#5571) with the machine whose folders or connectors it is.

MachineEnroll.description: machines/startEnroll (#1761): with as, a bot's machine code, an admin's only. Without, the caller's own, as before.

MachineFolderSend.description: machines/sendFolder, through machine/machines: one step of an agent's start_session with send (#2929), which sends this folder's branch to another of the person's machines first, or of its bring_back (#2947), which brings a branch back from there, or of its move_session (#3717), which moves a session there with its branch. Exactly one of state, upload, uploadSigned, receive, facts, pack, read, moveIn and seed; the control plane sends that machine's folders/receiveState, folders/receiveUpload, folders/receive, folders/sendFacts, folders/sendPack, folders/sendRead, agents/moveIn or folders/receiveSeed.

uploadSigned.description: true in place of upload (#7118): the step is folders/receiveUpload, and its part is only in the call's deliver, as this machine signed it, so a part's data goes to the control plane once. Needs a signed deliver of that method. Needs folders.signed-upload/1: an older control plane does not know it.

seed.description: The step is folders/receiveSeed (#7119). Needs folders.send-seed/1: an older control plane does not know it.

MachineFolderSent.description: What machines/sendFolder's step answered (#2929, #2947): state for state, folder for receive, facts for facts, pack for pack, read for read, seed for seed, none for upload. An upload or a read also says partsAtOnce.

partsAtOnce.description: How many parts of one file the sender may have in flight to or from that machine (#7120). None from an older control plane, and for a machine without folders.send-parts/1: one part at a time.

MachineHello.description: machine/hello, on every connect of an uplink. `implementation` is `swift` or `go` (#1134).

capabilities.description: The capabilities this host has (#1748): each one whose methods it all serves, and the ones it declares. None from a host older than #1748.

maturity.description: The levels of this host's capabilities that are not GA (#6579). None from a host older than that.

control.description: Where this machine's own control plane serves, when its install gave it the control role (agentsd install --control, #6610, #7313). Absent when it has none, and from an older host.

MachineHelloAnswer.description: The control plane's answer to machine/hello (#4100): what it can do, so the host asks only what it answers, such as machine/accounts with machine.accounts/1. An older control plane answers {}: no list, so the host asks it nothing new.

capabilities.description: The control plane's capabilities (#1748), as control/status says them to a client.

MachineInfo.description: One workspace, as its provider last listed it. `state` is running, starting, stopping, stopped or unknown; or failed, for a make that failed, with the provider's `reason` (#3972). `joining` while New Machine waits for it to join the control plane, and `notJoined` once the control plane gave up waiting (#4610). `setup` while it is being made (#6073).

addresses.description: Its public addresses, IPv4 then IPv6, from the provider's own record (#7466): an agent reaches root@<address> with the Agent Loops ssh key.

hostKeyRenews.description: Its ssh host key is made again at each start, as a Google Cloud workstation's is (#1701): after a Start the control plane made, the first ssh takes the key it is offered and pins it again.

idleTimeoutMinutes.description: The provider stops it by itself after this many minutes with no use, as GitHub stops a codespace (#4803): the machine's page says so.

reason.description: Why the make failed, in the provider's words, when `state` is failed.

joining.description: New Machine made it and the control plane waits for it to join: the row says Making… (#4610).

notJoined.description: Why the control plane gave up waiting for it to join, once it did (#4610): the row says so, with Delete.

setup.description: The set-up of a machine New Machine is making (#6073), from the press of Make until it joins (then its machine's row has it): what each step did, with its time, and on a failure the provider's words. A client that opens late reads where it is here.

MachineInstall.description: machines/install (MachineInstall.Request): a server over ssh, with its key, the fingerprint trusted, a tunnel. Add as Machine… names the provider and the workspace too (#3497): a codespace whose provider a machine carries is installed from that machine, with the token kept there.

MachineLink.description: machines/link. A machine whose ssh host key the control plane has not trusted yet (one that joined with the command, #3379) is refused -32069 hostKeyToTrust, data {fingerprint}, until trust is that fingerprint: the key is then kept for the machine's ssh start.

MachineMessagesError.description: A connector of messages/conversationsAll (#5571) that failed or did not answer in time, with its machine.

MachineProjects.description: projects/joined's answer and machine/projects (#2669): the projects that this machine's folders name, with their slots, all of them each time.

MachineRelease.description: machine/release (#2178): the release the control plane names, as X.Y.Z.

MachineSessionCall.description: machines/sessionCall, through machine/machines (#2927): an agent's read_session, message_session, stop_session, archive_session, or list_sessions and agent.ended wait status, on a session it started on another of the person's machines with start_session. The control plane sends that machine's agents/fromStarter, with call.from in its own words.

MachineSessionStart.description: machines/startSession, through machine/machines (#2887): an agent's start_session on another of the person's machines, by its name. The control plane sends that machine's agents/start.

MachineSetup.description: How a machine's set-up stands (#5355, epic #5353): the eight steps in order, and when it began and was ready. Steps 5 and 6 may run together.

MachineSetupDeliver.description: machines/setupDeliver through machine/machines (#7155): one of the person's machines, the sender, gives another of theirs a set-up script. The control plane sends that machine's setup/deliver as the sender signed it, and keeps nothing of the text.

host.description: The machine's id, as the person's lock names it.

last.description: The sender's last try (#7528): it does not send again when this one fails. The control plane then fails that machine's Your set-up, with the reason, when the step has not begun. Absent: a refusal as not in the lock is tried again.

MachineSetupProject.description: A project folder a pool machine gets: path is the folder on its sources, project the project id it joins there, and sources the person's machines that have it, those online first.

MachineSetupProjects.description: setup/projects: how the host's get of the pool's projects stands (#6890). pool is false for a machine no warm pool made, which gets none. finished with no problem: folders are the folders here.

MachineSetupReport.description: machine/setupStep: a step of the installer on the machine (agents-host install --join), as it starts, goes on and ends (#5355).

code.description: The digits the host shows for its join token (controllink.TokenCode), said with the compare step: the control plane compares them with the ones it made (#5359).

hash.description: The SHA-256, in lower-case hexadecimal, of the script that the root or user step runs (#7167).

warning.description: The step is done with a warning in its detail, such as a provider that cannot run root set-up (#7167).

MachineSetupStep.description: One step: detail is one line of what it is doing now or did; error is why it failed, in the words of the provider or the machine; fromPool says a warm pool did it before the machine was asked for; slower is true for a running step over 3 times its median (at least 2 minutes).

hash.description: The SHA-256, in lower-case hexadecimal, of the script that the root or user step runs (#7167).

warning.description: The step is done with a warning in its detail, such as a provider that cannot run root set-up (#7167).

MachineSetupStepID.description: The steps: create machine, join machine, install Agents, compare digits, install runtimes, send projects, sign in to runtimes, smoke session (#5353), and root set-up and your set-up, each only when its script was sent (#7167). The control plane reads a set-up by step id: a client that does not know an id shows it as its name.

MachineSetupWork.description: machine/setupWork: what the set-up of the machine that asks has left (#6890, #6896). pool: a warm pool made it. claimed: a person claimed it, and from is the first of steps 6 to 8 that waits to run (absent: none does now). done: nothing is left to ask for. projects: the project folders to get, at their last commit. An unclaimed machine does step 6 and stops. waitUser (#7416): Your set-up is on its way to this machine or runs there, and its projects wait for it: ask again.

MachineStatus.description: machine/status on channel 0 (#691 US4): each agent working or waiting on a person, and the next scheduled workflow.

MachineUpdate.description: machines/update (#1766): a host the control plane installed over ssh, updated the same way. The server and its key are given again, as at the install, because the control plane keeps neither; the host's own root and membership stay.

MachineVersions.description: machines/versions (#5272, spec 5239, "Alex's question"): the Agents versions a machine ran, from its machine/hello. version is the one it said last; firstSeen is the first time the control plane heard it at that version, and seen the last. deploys are the changes of version the control plane saw, newest first, at most 20: each an observed deploy (observed: true, state succeeded) of the component agents to the environment machines, its target labelled machine=<host>, from the last time the old version was seen (started) to the first machine/hello at the new one (finished). Each version's artifact is its commit: the tag vX.Y.Z for X.Y.Z, the sha after +g for X.Y.Z-dev.N+g<sha>. previous is the version it ran before version, when the control plane saw the change.

MemoryPressure.description: The kernel's memory pressure (#4578): macOS kern.memorystatus_vm_pressure_level, or Linux PSI memory (warn when some avg10 is 10% or more, critical when full avg10 is 10% or more).

MessagesConversationsAll.description: messages/conversationsAll (#5571): a page of conversations from the caller's machines, the newest first, each with its machine. errors says a connector that failed. unreached and notAsked are as in DocsListAll. cursor is the next page, absent at the end.

MessagesConversationsAllRequest.description: messages/conversationsAll (#5571): the conversations of the caller's machines in one call. limit is 1 to 100, 20 when not said; it bounds the page, not each machine, and a cursor goes with the same limit. unread: only the conversations with unread messages.

cursor.description: Opaque: the last page's cursor, as the answer gave it. Absent for the first page.

MoveAnswer.description: What a person's move came to. The message is what the window may show.

MoveNotification.description: move/changed (#4641): how a move to another machine goes, whoever asked for it. `sent` of `total` bytes of the branch are on that machine (0 of 0 while the bundle is made); `branchSent` once they are all there and the session itself goes; `finished` once it ended, whichever way: with no `problem` the session is there and gone from here, else `problem` says why it stopped, in the person's words, and the session stays here.

MoveRequest.description: The person moving an agent (053). No target takes back the person's move that is waiting.

MoveToMachineAnswer.description: What agents/moveToMachine did (#3790): the folder on that machine the session now goes on in, and whether it carries on there at once, as it was working when it moved.

MoveToMachineRequest.description: The person moving a session to another of their machines (#3790), as move_session does (#3717). `machine` is the control plane's id or name for it, and `machineName` the name the person knows it by, for the words; `folder` is an absolute path there, or, when left out, the folder of the session's project there.

PlaneMoveAction.description: What a client asks of a move of the control plane (#4255), as the Mac window's sheets do it: status says how it stands; move and return open Move to Another Machine… and Run It Here Again…; the rest are the sheets' buttons and the overview's.

PlaneMoveAsk.description: control/planeMove and control/planeMoveWanted (#4255): a client asks the window on the Mac that moves the control plane to do one step. The window does it with this Mac's control key, which never leaves the Mac.

address.description: With check on a move: where the other machine's control plane is, its https address; with no scheme, https.

PlaneMoveFlow.description: Where a move a client asked for is, as the Mac window's sheet would draw it (#4255), in its words.

kind.description: Move to Another Machine… or Run It Here Again….

step.description: The sheet's frame: key and check (P, Q or V), told (R or W), moving (S or X).

address.description: Where the control plane goes, or comes back from.

lines.description: The checks (key, check) or the stages (moving), in order.

members.description: Who has heard where it goes (told).

otherKey.description: Run It Here Again…: the other machine holds another key, so this Mac takes it first (Use Key…).

checked.description: Every check passed: Tell Everyone may be asked.

busy.description: A check or a step runs on the Mac now.

taken.description: The other end serves now: Cancel can't undo it.

failed.description: A stage failed: Close, not Cancel.

PlaneMoveLine.description: One check or stage of a move (#4255).

note.description: Why it failed, or a note under it.

PlaneMoveMember.description: A window, phone or machine of the control plane, and whether it knows where the control plane goes (#4255).

kind.description: What it is, and when it last connected, in words.

PlaneMoveRow.description: A row of the control plane's move card (#4255): Move to Another Machine, This Mac moved its control plane, a forwarding row, or the way back's.

confirm.description: Asked before the action, as Stop forwarding?'s message.

ProcessesState.description: processes/list (#3453): the machine's totals and the daemon's process tree, in tree order, the daemon first. At most 200 processes; omitted counts the rest.

ProjectMachine.description: A machine of projects/sessions (#3276) that has a folder of the project, by id and name.

ProjectMachineFolders.description: One machine of machines/projectFolders (#3277): its id and name, and the absolute paths of its folders in the project.

ProviderAdd.description: providers/add and providers/update. `machine` is the machine that carries the provider (#3398): it runs the provider's server, and `secrets` go on to it, never kept by the control plane. None picks the caller's first online machine; an update without it keeps the one it has.

ProviderCarried.description: What a provider's machine answers to providers/carry, providers/keepSecrets, providers/forget and providers/ssh (#3398): the call's result, or why it failed, in words for the person, and for a failure a client can act on, its `code` (#6072). Channel 0 has no error path.

code.description: Why it failed, for a client to say (#6072, W2b): denied (the person chose Deny), disconnected (the provider no longer takes the connection: it was removed there, or its refresh was refused), scope_missing (the person gave less than Agent Loops needs), account_inactive (the account can't make machines yet, such as no payment method), expired (the sign-in was not finished in time; start again), setup_script_changed (#7157: the person's root.sh is not the text a client of their lock approved for new machines, so the make stopped).

ProviderCarry.description: providers/carry (#3398): the control plane asks the machine that carries a provider to call it. `record` is the provider's record, which never holds a secret; the machine runs its server with the secrets it keeps. `secrets` is only those an add or an update was given to check with, for this call, and is not kept.

ProviderCreate.description: providers/create. With no `id`, the person's default provider: the first one added that they may make machines from (#3972). With no `name`, `machine-N`, from the person's own counter. With no `options`, the provider's defaults: each field's `default`, or else the first of its `enum`.

repository.description: The repository to start it from (#1809), an https git address. A provider whose New Machine form has `repository`, such as Codespaces, makes the workspace from it; any other has the host clone it once it joins, before `clones`.

ProviderOAuth.description: A provider connected with OAuth (#6072): whose account and team its machine's token is for, and whether the provider still takes it. Never a token.

account.description: The account's email, as the provider said at the connect.

team.description: The team the person chose on the provider's consent page.

state.description: disconnected: its last list was refused (the person removed Agent Loops at the provider, or its refresh failed): connect again.

ProviderOAuthCarried.description: providers/oauth's result in ProviderCarried (#6072): for start, the address to open and its state; for finish, whose account the token is for and the names of the secrets kept. Never a token.

ProviderOAuthCarry.description: providers/oauth (#6072): the control plane asks the machine that will carry a provider to start an OAuth connection (make and keep the PKCE verifier, about 10 minutes, and give the address to open) or to finish it (spend the code with the verifier, and keep the tokens for `provider` in ~/.agents-secrets). The verifier and the tokens never leave that machine.

origin.description: start: the web page's origin, for the hand-back page; none for the Mac and the Remote.

error.description: finish: the provider's error from the callback, such as access_denied.

ProviderOAuthFinish.description: providers/oauthFinish (#6072): what the hand-back page gave the client (the code and the state, or the provider's error). The machine that started it spends the code; the control plane then adds the provider (or, with the `id` of one it started for, connects it again) with no secret of its own.

name.description: The new provider's name; none is the preset's provider's name, such as DigitalOcean.

ProviderOAuthStart.description: providers/oauthStart (#6072): connect a provider with OAuth instead of a pasted token. `machine` carries it (the caller's first online one when none); `id` connects an existing provider again; `origin` is the web page's.

ProviderOAuthStarted.description: providers/oauthStart's result: the provider's consent page to open (in ASWebAuthenticationSession, or a new window on the web), its state, and the machine that will keep the connection.

ProviderOptions.description: providers/options: the New Machine form, a JSON Schema, with what New Machine would make (#4634). With no `id`, the person's default provider.

id.description: The provider the form is for: the one asked for, or else the person's default.

values.description: The values the form starts with: the options the person made a machine with last on this provider, over each field's `default` or else the first of its `enum`.

name.description: The name New Machine would give: the person's next `machine-N`. Not kept until a make uses it.

ProviderRequest.description: providers/remove, providers/refresh, providers/options (with no `id`, the default provider).

ProviderSSH.description: providers/ssh (#3398): the machine that carries a codespaces provider starts a codespace's agentsd over ssh (`start`), reads its host key (`hostKey`), installs Agents in it with a host code from the control plane (`install`, #3497), or holds an ssh session to it that GitHub counts as use while its machine works (`keepAwake`, renewed each few minutes, and `letSleep`, #4637), with the token it keeps. Its result is ProviderSSHResult.

hostCode.description: install's host code: the codespace runs the control plane's install.sh with it, from the address and pin it names.

ProviderSSHResult.description: providers/ssh's result (#3398): the host key taken, in known_hosts form, and for hostKey a fingerprint to trust first.

ProviderSummary.description: A provider for the Providers page, never its commands, headers or secrets' values.

group.description: The group whose users may use it (#1761); none is the admins' alone.

mayUse.description: The caller may start machines from it (#1761): they are in its group. Absent from an older control plane, which lets everyone.

default.description: New Machine makes the caller's machines on it (#3979): the one they made a machine on last or chose with Make Default, or else the first one added. True on one provider at most; absent from an older control plane.

machine.description: The machine that carries it: runs its server and keeps its secrets (#3398). Absent for one made before, which must be added again.

machineOffline.description: Its machine is offline: its machines can't be started, stopped, made or deleted until it is back (#3398).

sshToolMissing.description: The CLI its machines are reached through over ssh (gh, coder) when the control plane's machine has none (#3367). Absent when it needs none or has it.

oauth.description: It is connected with OAuth (#6072), not a pasted token: whose account, and whether the connection still works. Absent for a pasted token.

ReceiveRequest.description: Makes or brings up to date a host's copy of a Mac's repository (#1123): fetches the `bundle` upload, moves `branches` forward only, checks out `checkout`, sets `origin`, applies the `patch` upload (uncommitted changes), and adds the folder as a folder. It stops, and changes nothing, when the host has changes or commits of its own.

seed.description: The folders/receiveSeed (#7119) whose commits a new folder starts from. Needs folders.seed/1, which the machine showed with its answer to the seed.

ReceiveSeed.description: How a seed (folders/receiveSeed, #7119) stands. `done` bytes came from the origin. Once `finished`: `heads` are the commits that the send can leave out of its bundle, or `problem` says why there are none, and the send carries everything.

ReceiveSeedRequest.description: folders/receiveSeed (#7119): the machine gets the commits of a send from `origin`, before the send. `seed` is an id of the sender's own: its first call starts the seed, and each later one says how it stands. A folder that is there fetches its own origin, when that is the same repository; a new one is fetched beside, and folders/receive with `seed` starts the folder from it, so a seed makes no folder. `origin` holds no credential. `stop` ends the seed and drops what it got.

ReceiveState.description: What a host has at a folder before a send (#1123). `heads` are the commits of its branches and of its newest remote-tracking branches (#7119), so the Mac's bundle carries only what the host lacks. `ownChanges` is true when the folder has changes that the last send did not put there.

ReceiveStateRequest.description: Asks a host about a folder a Mac will send a repository to (Send to ‹host›…, #1123). `folder` may start with ~/.

ReceiveUploadRequest.description: One part of a file a Mac sends (#1123), at `offset` in the upload. The part at 0 comes first; the others come in any order (#7120). A part is at most 16 MB; the host keeps the upload until folders/receive uses it.

RequiredCapabilities.description: What the control plane needs of a peer to route for it (#1748): a host without each of host is needsUpdate, and a client without each of client is answered -32008.

accountFolderVariable.description: The variable that names the folder its sign-in is kept in, for a runtime that can have more than one account (#840): CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, CODEX_HOME.

setBy.description: Set when the organisation's policy does not allow this runtime here (#998, FR-010).

version.description: The installed copy's version: the toolset's pinned version for the app's own copy, else what the runtime's --version says (#3674). Absent when it is not installed or does not say.

SSHHost.description: A server ssh knows by a name, for Add a Machine's server box (#610).

SSHHostsRequest.description: machines/sshHosts (#610): with a destination, just that, as typed.

SelfUpdate.description: How a Mac's host updates Agents Host to the release the control plane names, with no administrator (#2178).

release.description: The release the control plane named last; none until it names one.

message.description: Why it failed or cannot, in a sentence for the person.

SelfUpdateState.description: Where updating Agents Host is (#2178): upToDate, off (the person turned it off), downloading, waiting (ready; it waits for the last turn to end), restarting, failed (the next release named tries again), cannot (this copy cannot update itself, such as one in a folder only an administrator changes).

SendFacts.description: What the Send sheet shows (#1123): the local branches, the one checked out (none when detached), the origin, and whether anything is uncommitted.

untracked.description: The files git neither tracks nor ignores, when `measureUntracked` asked and there are some (#7121).

SendFactsRequest.description: Asks this Mac's host about a repository to send (Send to ‹host›…, #1123).

measureUntracked.description: Measures the untracked files too, with a bound (#7121). Only the Send sheet asks.

SendFile.description: A file the host made for a send, read with folders/sendRead (#1123).

SendNotification.description: send/changed (#4613): how a send that folders/send started goes. `sent` of `total` bytes are on the other machine (0 of 0 while the bundle is made); `finished` once it ended, whichever way: `received` is the folder it became there, or `problem` says why it stopped, in the person's words.

SendPack.description: What folders/sendPack made (#1123): each branch at its commit, the bundle (none when the receiving host has every commit) and the patch (none when nothing is uncommitted).

SendPackRequest.description: Makes what a send carries (#1123): a bundle of `branches` without the commits in `leavingOut` (the receiving host's), and with `includeChanges` a patch of the uncommitted changes, new files git does not ignore among them.

leaveOutUntracked.description: With `includeChanges`, leaves out the files git does not track (#7121). Absent is false: they go.

SendRead.description: A part of at most 4 MB (#7120); 1 MB for an export (#1530). `end` is true for the last, and then the host removes the file.

SendReadRequest.description: One part of a file folders/sendPack made, from `offset` (#1123).

SendRequest.description: folders/send (#4613): Send to ‹machine›… from a client. This host sends `branches` of the repository at `folder`, less the commits the folder there has, and with `includeChanges` its uncommitted changes, to `destination` on `machine` (the control plane's id or name for it; `machineName` is the name the person knows it by, for the words), through the control plane, as start_session with send does (#2929). There `checkout` is checked out and `origin` set.

leaveOutUntracked.description: With `includeChanges`, leaves out the files git does not track (#7121). Absent is false: they go.

SendSummary.description: One send folders/send started (#4613): the folder here, and the folder on the machine it goes to.

SendUntracked.description: What a send of the uncommitted changes takes of files git neither tracks nor ignores (#7121): how many, their bytes, and the largest folders. `partial` when the measure stopped at its bound, so there is more; `buildOutput` when some are in a folder named as build output is (node_modules, build, .build, DerivedData, target, dist).

SendUntrackedItem.description: An untracked folder (its path ends in /) or file of SendUntracked, from the repository's top, and its bytes.

SentBranch.description: A branch the Mac sends, at the commit it has (#1123).

SessionMoveIn.description: agents/moveIn (#3717): a session moving here from another of the person's machines, with move_session. `upload` is the export of its record and its transcript, sent with folders/receiveUpload; `folder` is the folder here it goes on in, where its branch was sent first. It keeps its id, labels and times, and goes on in this machine's root; its runtime reads the app's record ahead of its next prompt (`movedFrom`). `from` is the machine it leaves (the control plane writes `machine`), and the agent there that started it, when that agent stays there. With `carryOn`, it starts again here at once, as it was working when it moved.

SessionMovedFrom.description: The machine a session moved here from with move_session (#3717), and when.

SetupApprove.description: setup/approve (#7167): a client of the person's lock approves the text of one of this machine's set-up scripts as it is now, for machines as they are made (scope made) or for one machine (m:<id>). approval is a setup.script record whose subject is script and whose content is the script's hash and size; empty content takes the approval of that scope away. The machine keeps the text and the approval only when the record checks against its lock, its number is not lower than the last of its scope, and the file is that text.

SetupDeliver.description: setup/deliver (#7155, gate 1 of #7151, section 3): a machine of the person's lock, the sender, gives this machine a set-up script with its approval, signed for this machine. This machine takes it only by the four rules of section 3 (setupdelivery.go), keeps it in <root>/machine-setup.json, and runs it as its user, as the step user (Your set-up). made: an automatic send to a machine as it is made or claimed, with an approval of scope made, which a machine takes once.

SetupRootAgain.description: setup/rootAgain (#7159): read root.sh's result on this machine again.

rest.description: Then run the steps after Root set-up too, as Try Again does after it failed.

SetupRootCommand.description: setup/rootCommand (#7159): the command a person runs as root on a machine that cannot run root.sh by itself, such as their own server or a made machine whose root.sh failed. It runs the root.sh that a client approved for made machines, once, and leaves its result where Root set-up reads it.

command.description: One line to paste in a terminal there: the script in base64, run with sudo.

hash.description: The hash of the root.sh it runs.

SetupRootLog.description: setup/rootLog (#7159): this machine's root.log, from its last root.sh run, for Show Log.

text.description: The end of root.log, at most 64 KiB; empty when there is none.

cut.description: The log is longer, and text is only its end.

SetupScript.description: One set-up script on this machine (#7167): root (root.sh) or setup (setup.sh) in ~/.agents/machine-setup/. present: the file is there. text, hash and size are the file as it is now (hash: SHA-256 in lower-case hexadecimal); problem says why they are absent from a file that is there (over its limit, or unreadable). approvedText and approvedHash are the text a client approved last, and approvals the records in force for it, one a scope. changed: the file is not the approved text, so it is not used until a client approves it. nextSeq is the number to sign the next approval with.

SetupScripts.description: setup/scripts (#7167): this machine's two set-up scripts, root then setup, as a client reads them to approve one.

folder.description: The folder the scripts are in, ~/.agents/machine-setup/ of this machine's personal home, as an absolute path (#7512): Settings ▸ Machines ▸ Machine scripts opens it and writes an example there. Left out when the machine has no personal home (a scratch root), which has no scripts.

SetupSend.description: setup/send (#7155, gate 1 of #7151, section 3): Send Set-up. A client of the person's lock asks this machine, the sender, to send its setup.sh to the machine host and run it there. approval is a setup.script record of setup, scope m:<host>, of the file as it is now: the sender keeps it as setup/approve does, then sends the approved text, signed by this machine for host, through the control plane (machines/setupDeliver). It answers when host took it, which then runs it.

host.description: The machine's id, as the person's lock names it.

SetupWanted.description: setup/wanted (#7155): the control plane asks the machine that carries a provider whether it sends the person's setup.sh to a machine it made (or a warm pool's machine that a person claimed). It carries no text; the sender sends it only with an approval of scope made, and the target takes one such send.

SetupWantedAnswer.description: setup/wanted's answer (#7416): sending says that the sender has a setup.sh approved for new machines, and sends it now.

summary.description: The command and its first arguments, or the URL without its query.

clash.description: The runtimes with a server of this name in their own config, and that file.

Simulator.description: An iOS simulator on a Mac host (#842): its UDID, its name, its system and whether it is booted.

SimulatorList.description: simulators/list: the host's simulators, booted first. Reason says why there are none to list, when a host has no simulators (not a Mac, no Xcode).

SimulatorRequest.description: simulators/boot and simulators/shutdown: one simulator, by its UDID.

SimulatorScreen.description: A booted simulator's screen as a JPEG, and its size in pixels.

SimulatorScreenRequest.description: simulators/screen: a booted simulator's screen, at most maxHeight pixels tall (1200 when left out).

SimulatorTapRequest.description: simulators/tap: a touch on a booted simulator's screen, where from 0 to 1 across (x) and down (y).

StartedMachinePreview.description: A started machine in people/removePreview: the branches and worktrees on it with work that is not pushed. `unknown` says why it could not be asked (offline, or it did not answer), and then `unpushed` is empty.

WakeSettings.description: Whether this Mac is kept awake for agents, and for how long after they stop (024), as wake.json in the settings of the person (#6745).

warmRuntimes.description: How many finished sessions keep their runtime running, ready for a reply (#183, #4044): 0 to 8, default 3, 0 turning the warm pool off. A runtime with background processes does not count against it.

backgroundHours.description: How long a finished runtime whose background processes (a dev server, a build, a watcher) still run is kept, counted from its last turn's end (#4044): 1 to 24 hours, default 4. Its processes are then ended with it. 0, or missing, from a client that does not know it, keeps the value the host has.

releaseAfterMinutes.description: How long a finished runtime with no background processes is kept, counted from its last turn's end, before the host ends it (#4044, #4513): 0 to 1440 minutes, default 10. An agent that waits for an event (wait_for_event, a lease) is then continued with session/load when the event comes. 0 releases none for being idle; warmRuntimes still holds. Missing, from a client that does not know it, keeps the value the host has. A runtime that can neither load nor resume a conversation is kept while its agent waits.

WakeState.description: Why the Mac is, or is not, being kept awake (024).

WarmPool.description: A warm pool (#5363, epic #5353, Part 2 of the machine set-up spec): a provider's machines kept made, joined, with Agents, runtimes and the pool's projects at their last commit, and signed in to nothing. minReady is what it keeps; maxSize is the most it holds, ready or being set up (a claimed machine leaves the pool and does not count). target is written by the control plane and is minReady until auto-scale. ready, settingUp, failedMakes, stoppedBecause and waitingBecause are read-only. machines and claims are read-only too (#5366).

provider.description: The machine provider's id: only a provider can make machines.

runtimes.description: The runtimes to install; none means those of the pool's projects.

projects.description: The project folders to send, at their last commit.

minReady.description: Machines kept ready (set up, unclaimed). 0 makes nothing. At most maxSize.

maxSize.description: The most machines held at once, ready or being set up. At least 1.

target.description: What the pool aims at: minReady, until auto-scale writes it.

replaceAfter.description: Seconds after which a ready machine is replaced. Default 86400 (24 hours).

failedMakes.description: Makes that failed in a row. Three stop the pool.

stoppedBecause.description: Why the pool stopped making, in the provider's words.

review.description: The script the pool waits for the person to review (#7157): root when the machine that carries its provider refused a make because root.sh is not the text a client of the person's lock approved for new machines (code setup_script_changed). The pool is stopped until a pool/set with reviewed. Read-only.

waitingBecause.description: Why a pool that is keeping makes no machine now: no machine that has its projects is online (#6890).

machines.description: The machines the pool holds now, ready, setting up or failed (#5366): a line each on the pool's card.

WarmPoolClaim.description: pool/claim (#5365, #5366): New Machine's Start from a warm pool. The oldest ready machine of a pool of this provider and size, bound to the person with their Stop when idle; with none ready, a new machine.

stopWhenIdle.description: Minutes; 0 is never. Absent keeps the machine's.

WarmPoolClaimed.description: What pool/claim gave: a pool's machine (fromPool, with its host) or a new machine being made, with note saying so.

host.description: The machine's host id; absent for a new machine, which joins on its own.

pool.description: The pool's name, when it came from one.

WarmPoolClaims.description: A pool's claims in the last seven days (#5366): how many, how many found it empty and fell back to a new machine, and the median time from a claim to the machine being ready, when any is.

WarmPoolHours.description: When a pool runs: on these weekdays (0 Sunday to 6 Saturday) from `from` to `to`, as HH:MM in `timezone` (an IANA name; UTC when absent). Outside them the ready machines are deleted and none are made. A pool with no hours runs every day.

WarmPoolMachine.description: One machine a warm pool holds (#5366).

detail.description: What its set-up is doing now, as the running step's line says: installing Claude.

WarmPoolScope.description: Whose pool it is. Only user is built (#5353).

WarmPoolSet.description: pool/set: makes a pool, or changes the one with this id. The control plane writes target, state and the counts. Min must not be above max, and max is at least 1.

reviewed.description: The person approved the pool's changed root.sh (#7157): the pool makes machines again, and replaces its unclaimed machines made before now, which ran the older text.

WarmPoolState.description: keeping: the pool makes and replaces. off-hours: outside its hours. stopped: three makes failed in a row, see stoppedBecause. empty: minReady is 0.

WebPagePairing.description: machine/pairWebPage (#4214): the web page's address with a one-time browser code after #code=, for the agent browser to open.

WebServe.description: control/setWeb (#4252, 071 FR-002): serve Agents to browsers on the control plane's Mac, or stop. Off closes the loopback listener; a page open through it stays connected.
